author: Mark Atwood
text:
Update from /do-beads JMAP-jfia 2026-05-16 investigation:

The 2026-05-15 comment claimed crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mdn.rs:462-466 has a live wire-leak that should be filed against jmap-mail-server. On careful re-read of the actual code, **that claim is incorrect**. The mdn.rs handler at lines 485-489 already uses `server_fail_from_backend(&inner)` / `server_fail_from_backend(&se)` — the redaction helper from jmap-server::handlers — which returns JmapError::server_fail(SERVER_FAIL_INTERNAL_DESC) and drops the Display string. No live leak exists.

A workspace-wide grep for `BackendSetError::Other(e) =>` across crate-jmap-mail-server/src/ found 25 call sites; ALL use server_fail_from_backend or server_fail_value_from_backend. No call site interpolates the Display directly.

**However**, the stale trait-doc at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:230 prescribes the leak pattern verbatim:
    | `Err(BackendSetError::Other(e))` | `notCreated[creationId] = { type: "serverFail", description: <e.to_string()> }` |

This is the most likely path to a future leak — a contributor adding a new backend method or new module copies the prescribed pattern. Filed as bd:JMAP-atwe (P1) with the workspace canonical-template sweep across the 7 sibling *-server crates.

The .36 structural decision (BackendSetError::into_set_error_or_method_error or equivalent surface on the foundation crate) remains a genuine human-judgment call — it's foundation-crate API addition with the security-boundary high-stakes qualifier from workspace AGENTS.md 'When NOT to file human' rule #3. Keeping the human label. The .36 author's 2026-05-15 'releasing claim, want sign-off' note still stands.

Bead remains open with human label. The follow-up bd:JMAP-atwe (stale doc fix) is independently actionable and not blocked on .36's decision.
